newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PHILIPS TO AUCTION TSMC SHARES.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS TO AUCTION TSMC SHARES.

text.p: Philips Taiwan, a fully-owned subsidiary of Philips Electronics NV, said on Tuesday it would auction 100 million shares of microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co later this month.
"We plan to auction off 100 million shares on August 18," Denise Sun, the firm's spokeswoman, told Reuters.
After the auction, Philips' stake in Taiwan Semiconductor would be reduced by two percent to around 31 percent, Sun said.
Philips has commissioned Capital Securities to launch the auction, she added.
The base price at which shares would be auctioned would not be set until August 18, she said. On Tuesday, Taiwan Semiconductor closed up T$2 at T$153.
Minimum bid would be 10,000 shares, with the maximum at five million shares, she said.
Sun said at the moment Philips had no concrete plan for further auctions of the chip giant's shares.
Philips Taiwan, the largest foreign firm on the island, is Philips group's regional operation centre, producing cathode ray tubes, computer monitors, integrated circuits testing and packaging.
